appraisal_events.evidence: « Quelle différence avec Forcheville ! Voilà au moins un homme qui vous dit carrément sa façon de penser... il est toujours comte de Forcheville, ajouta-t-il d'un air délicat, comme si... il en soupesait minutieusement la valeur particulière. »
appraisal_events.explanation: M. Verdurin praises Forcheville's frankness and title in explicit contrast to Swann, but the narrator's aside mocking his pretended expertise about the count's rank undercuts the seriousness of this elevation.

appraisal_events.evidence: « comme il a vu que Brichot était aimé dans la maison, c'était une manière de nous atteindre »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin's complaint asserts, in passing, that Brichot is affectionately regarded within the household, marking him as securely valued in the salon independent of the attack on Swann.

status_effects.explanation: Held up by M. Verdurin as the frank, titled counter-example to Swann, though the narrator's ironic framing tempers how much weight this praise should carry.
Asserted to be affectionately regarded ('aimé') within the Verdurin household, a mark of secure inclusion in the valued social space.

ambiguities: M. Verdurin's praise of Forcheville's title is narrated with visible irony ('comme si... il en soupesait minutieusement la valeur particulière'), suggesting the narrator views the elevation as pretentious rather than substantive; this is reflected in reduced confidence rather than omission.

Odette's stated preference for Forcheville ('Odette a l'air de préférer joliment le Forcheville, et je lui donne raison') was not scored as a distinct event because Odette functions here as the source of a preference rather than as the target of praise or blame; her preference mainly serves to reinforce Forcheville's local elevation (captured in S1) rather than positioning her own status.
